correctness.rationale: The rank-five simple-cycle equivalence threshold nineteen is Theorem 4.9 of Brown–Hoshino (2007). Replacing squared adjacency by nonloop original adjacency or a length-two path increases quantifier rank by at most one, proving the infinite tail. For n=5..19, the exact recursive tuple type (atomic diagram, set of all one-vertex extension types) distinguishes all fifteen, and its correctness follows by induction on quantifier rank. A full labeled-tuple C++ implementation and a dihedral-orbit C++ implementation independently agree for n=5..32, with extra orbit tests through n=72. The finite tests are not being extrapolated to all n.

originality.rationale: The nearest published cycle theorem covers the infinite tail as a corollary but does not classify the exceptional square graphs at rank four. The exact fifteen-class, sharp nineteen-vertex statement was not found in direct equivalent, broader and table searches. The 2012 cycle-power paper and 1989 induced-subgraph paper address different invariants. A previous rank-three classification of cycle powers leaves the additional rank-four distinctions unresolved. Historical priority is qualified by incomplete coverage of older or unindexed work.
residual_risks: No exhaustive search of every unindexed historical work has been carried out; a preexisting equivalent classification could exist.

value.rationale: An exact classification of ordinary first-order bounded-rank theories for a natural four-regular circulant graph family, with a sharp representative bound. The gap between induced four-vertex pattern stabilization at size twelve and complete rank-four stabilization at nineteen is a mathematically motivated expressiveness distinction. The result refines the rank-three picture and combines a nontrivial finite boundary classification with a general interpretation transfer; neither mere experiment nor a known-table recomputation.
